title: Paris
content: Home to the Louvre, Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower, with café-lined boulevards and riverbanks made for walking.

title: Rome
content: Two and a half thousand years of layered history, from the Colosseum and Forum to the Vatican and Trevi Fountain.

title: Tokyo
content: A vast, orderly metropolis pairing neon districts and shrines with some of the best food anywhere on earth.

title: London
content: Royal palaces, world-class free museums, theatres and markets in a city shaped by two thousand years of history.

title: New York City
content: Skyscrapers, Central Park, Broadway and museums packed into five boroughs that reward days of exploring.

title: Barcelona
content: Gaudí's Sagrada Família and Park Güell, a Gothic Quarter, city beaches and a lively tapas and market scene.

title: Istanbul
content: A city on two continents, with Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, the Grand Bazaar and ferries across the Bosphorus.

title: Kyoto
content: Japan's former capital holds around 1,600 temples, geisha districts, bamboo groves and traditional tea houses.

title: Prague
content: A remarkably intact medieval centre of spires, Charles Bridge and a hilltop castle above the Vltava river.

title: Amsterdam
content: Canal rings, the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Anne Frank House make a compact, bike-friendly city break.

title: Vienna
content: Imperial palaces, grand coffee houses and a world-leading classical music tradition on the Danube.

title: Lisbon
content: Hilly, tiled and sunlit, with Alfama's alleys, yellow trams, custard tarts and views over the Tagus estuary.

title: Florence
content: The cradle of the Renaissance, home to the Uffizi, Michelangelo's David and Brunelleschi's great dome.

title: Venice
content: A car-free city built on a lagoon, with the Grand Canal, St Mark's Basilica and the Doge's Palace.

title: Singapore
content: A clean, green island city-state known for Gardens by the Bay, hawker centres and a mix of Chinese, Malay and Indian cultures.

title: Hong Kong
content: Dense skyscrapers set against green hills and harbour, with dim sum, night markets and the Peak tram.

title: Sydney
content: A harbour city with the Opera House, Harbour Bridge and Bondi Beach within easy reach of each other.

title: Cape Town
content: Table Mountain rises over beaches, vineyards and the Cape Peninsula, with Robben Island nearby.

title: Buenos Aires
content: Tango halls, grand European-style avenues, steakhouses and the colourful streets of La Boca and Recoleta.

title: Rio de Janeiro
content: Copacabana and Ipanema beaches sit beneath Sugarloaf Mountain and the Christ the Redeemer statue.

title: Marrakesh
content: The red city of souks, riads and the Jemaa el-Fnaa square, with the Atlas Mountains on the horizon.

title: Dubai
content: Home to the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, plus huge malls, desert safaris and man-made islands.

title: Bangkok
content: Gilded temples, river boats, street food and markets in Thailand's energetic capital.

title: Seoul
content: Royal palaces and hanok villages sit alongside K-pop culture, fast tech and outstanding Korean barbecue.

title: San Francisco
content: The Golden Gate Bridge, cable cars, Alcatraz and steep, colourful streets above a fog-prone bay.

title: Edinburgh
content: A castle-topped volcanic skyline, a medieval Old Town and Georgian New Town, and the world's largest arts festival.

title: Budapest
content: Two cities on the Danube, with thermal baths, a Parliament building and ruin bars in the old Jewish quarter.

title: Copenhagen
content: Colourful Nyhavn, Tivoli Gardens, cycling culture and a leading reputation for New Nordic dining.

title: Berlin
content: A city of living history, from the Brandenburg Gate and Berlin Wall remnants to galleries, clubs and Museum Island.

title: Madrid
content: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Retiro Park anchor a city famed for late-night tapas and lively plazas.

title: Athens
content: The Acropolis and Parthenon overlook a city that holds the origins of democracy, plus tavernas in Plaka.

title: Cairo
content: Africa's largest city sits beside the Giza pyramids and the Sphinx, with a vast Egyptian Museum collection.

title: Mexico City
content: Built on an Aztec island capital, with Zócalo, Frida Kahlo's house, grand museums and exceptional street food.

title: Vancouver
content: Mountains, forest and ocean meet in a relaxed Pacific city with Stanley Park and strong Asian food.

title: Cusco
content: The old Inca capital at 3,400 metres, with Spanish colonial streets and the gateway to Machu Picchu.

title: Hanoi
content: A thousand-year-old capital of lakes, French colonial buildings, a tangled Old Quarter and superb street food.

title: Hoi An
content: A lantern-lit ancient trading port with preserved wooden merchant houses, tailors and riverside cafés.

title: Siem Reap
content: The base for visiting the temples of Angkor, including Angkor Wat, one of the world's largest religious monuments.

title: Luang Prabang
content: A UNESCO-listed town of golden temples at the meeting of the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers, known for dawn alms rounds.

title: Salzburg
content: Mozart's birthplace is a baroque city below a fortress, set against the Alps and famed for The Sound of Music.

title: Munich
content: Beer halls, Marienplatz, the Alps nearby and top museums in Bavaria's confident capital.

title: Dublin
content: Georgian squares, the Book of Kells, literary pubs and the Guinness Storehouse in a friendly, walkable capital.

title: Stockholm
content: Spread across 14 islands, with a Gamla Stan old town, the Vasa warship museum and a long archipelago.

title: Oslo
content: A fjord-side capital with the Viking Ship Museum, a striking opera house and quick access to forest and sea.

title: Helsinki
content: Design, neoclassical architecture, saunas and sea fortress island Suomenlinna in a compact Baltic capital.

title: Tallinn
content: One of Europe's best-preserved medieval old towns, with walls, towers and a lively tech-minded modern side.

title: Kraków
content: A grand market square, Wawel Castle and the Kazimierz district, with Auschwitz and a salt mine within reach.

title: Dubrovnik
content: A walled Adriatic port with limestone streets, city walls you can walk and Game of Thrones filming locations.

title: Seville
content: Flamenco, orange trees, the Alcázar and a vast cathedral in Andalusia's hot, tile-covered capital.

title: Granada
content: The Alhambra palace sits above the Albaicín quarter, with free tapas and the Sierra Nevada behind.

title: Porto
content: Tiled churches, steep riverside lanes and port wine lodges across the Douro from Vila Nova de Gaia.

title: Naples
content: The birthplace of pizza sits in the shadow of Vesuvius, close to Pompeii and a superb archaeological museum.

title: Milan
content: Italy's fashion and design capital, with the Duomo, La Scala and Leonardo's The Last Supper.

title: Bruges
content: A preserved medieval canal city of cobbles, belfry and chocolate shops, easily seen on foot in a weekend.

title: Brussels
content: The Grand-Place, art nouveau townhouses, comics murals, chocolate, waffles and a huge beer culture.

title: Zürich
content: A lakeside old town with clean air, chocolate and watches, set between mountains and the Limmat river.

title: Geneva
content: A lakeside city with the Jet d'Eau, a cluster of international organisations and views to Mont Blanc.

title: Lyon
content: France's gastronomic capital, with bouchon restaurants, Roman remains and a Renaissance old town.

title: Bordeaux
content: A grand 18th-century riverside city at the heart of the world's most famous wine region.

title: Nice
content: The Promenade des Anglais, a colourful old town and Matisse and Chagall museums on the French Riviera.

title: Glasgow
content: Victorian and art nouveau architecture, the Kelvingrove museum, live music and a strong Mackintosh legacy.

title: Valletta
content: A tiny fortified capital of honey-coloured baroque buildings, with St John's Co-Cathedral and harbour views.

title: Reykjavík
content: The world's northernmost capital, a base for geothermal pools, the Northern Lights and the Golden Circle.

title: Jerusalem
content: The Old City holds sites sacred to three faiths, including the Western Wall, Church of the Holy Sepulchre and Dome of the Rock.

title: Petra
content: A rose-red city carved into canyon walls by the Nabataeans, reached through the narrow Siq gorge.

title: Muscat
content: A calm, white-washed Gulf capital with the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque, a harbour souk and mountains behind.

title: Abu Dhabi
content: The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Louvre Abu Dhabi and Yas Island sit within one of the Gulf's wealthiest cities.

title: Fez
content: Home to the world's oldest continuously operating university and a huge car-free medina of tanneries and craft workshops.

title: Zanzibar City
content: Stone Town's alleyways, carved doors and spice-trade history sit beside Indian Ocean beaches.

title: Nairobi
content: Africa's only capital with a national park on its edge, where lions and giraffes can be seen against the skyline.

title: Mumbai
content: India's film and finance capital, with the Gateway of India, colonial Gothic buildings and street snacks.

title: Delhi
content: Mughal monuments such as Red Fort and Humayun's Tomb stand alongside colonial avenues and busy bazaars.

title: Jaipur
content: The Pink City, with Amber Fort, the City Palace and Hawa Mahal on the Golden Triangle route.

title: Agra
content: Home to the Taj Mahal, built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife, and the red sandstone Agra Fort.

title: Varanasi
content: One of the world's oldest living cities, where pilgrims bathe and perform rites on the ghats of the Ganges.

title: Kathmandu
content: A valley of temples and stupas, including Boudhanath and Swayambhunath, and the usual start point for Himalayan treks.

title: Beijing
content: The Forbidden City, Temple of Heaven and Tiananmen Square, with the Great Wall within a day trip.

title: Shanghai
content: The Bund's colonial waterfront faces the futuristic skyline of Pudong, with gardens and strong dumplings.

title: Xi'an
content: The ancient Silk Road capital, guarding the Terracotta Army and a complete Ming dynasty city wall.

title: Taipei
content: Night markets, hot springs, a thriving tea and café culture and the Taipei 101 tower.

title: Osaka
content: Japan's kitchen, famed for street food in Dotonbori and takoyaki, with a castle and a lively nightlife.

title: Hiroshima
content: The Peace Memorial Park and Atomic Bomb Dome offer a moving history, with Miyajima island close by.

title: Kuala Lumpur
content: The Petronas Towers rise above a multicultural food scene and the Batu Caves Hindu shrine.

title: Chiang Mai
content: A walled northern Thai city with over 300 temples, night bazaars, cooking schools and elephant sanctuaries.

title: Ho Chi Minh City
content: Scooters, French colonial landmarks, the War Remnants Museum and the Cu Chi tunnels in Vietnam's southern hub.

title: Melbourne
content: Laneway cafés, street art, sport and a leading coffee scene make this Australia's cultural capital.

title: Auckland
content: Built across volcanic cones between two harbours, with islands, wineries and beaches within easy reach.

title: Queenstown
content: New Zealand's adventure capital on Lake Wakatipu, surrounded by mountains and gateway to Milford Sound.

title: Toronto
content: The CN Tower, Kensington Market and a diverse food scene, with Niagara Falls an easy day trip away.

title: Montreal
content: A French-speaking city of cobbled Old Montreal, festivals, bagels and a strong cafe culture.

title: Quebec City
content: North America's only walled city north of Mexico, with the Château Frontenac and a fortified old quarter.

title: Chicago
content: Pioneering skyscraper architecture, deep-dish pizza, the Art Institute and a lakefront park system.

title: New Orleans
content: Jazz, Creole food and the French Quarter, plus Mardi Gras, in one of the most distinctive US cities.

title: Boston
content: The Freedom Trail links colonial sites, and Harvard and MIT sit across the river in Cambridge.

title: Washington, D.C.
content: Free Smithsonian museums, the National Mall, the White House and the Lincoln Memorial.

title: Los Angeles
content: Hollywood, Venice Beach, Getty Center and Griffith Observatory spread across a car-led sprawl.

title: Las Vegas
content: The Strip's themed casinos, shows and neon, with the Grand Canyon and Hoover Dam in reach.

title: Havana
content: Classic American cars, crumbling colonial grandeur, salsa and the Malecón seafront in the Cuban capital.

title: Cartagena
content: A walled Caribbean port of pastel balconies and plazas, with warm evenings and colonial fortress San Felipe de Barajas.

title: Lima
content: Peru's capital is a leading South American food destination, with colonial centre and Pacific clifftop views.
